title: Interest on a Loan
devanagari: मासे शतस्य यदि पञ्च कलान्तरं स्यात्
वर्षे गते भवति किं वद षोडशानाम्।
translation: If the interest on 100 is 5 a month, tell me the interest on 16 when a year has passed. And, O mathematician, tell me how to find the time from the principal and the interest, and the principal when you know the time and the interest.
translation_hi: यदि 100 पर एक महीने का ब्याज 5 हो, तो बताओ कि एक वर्ष बीतने पर 16 पर कितना ब्याज होगा। और हे गणितज्ञ, मूलधन और ब्याज से समय, तथा समय और ब्याज जानकर मूलधन भी बताओ।

words.note: Locative of masa. Hindi मास, महीना.
Genitive plural of shodasha. Hindi सोलह.
Literally 'root'. The root of the money, like the root of a number!
phala = fruit, result: the interest earned.

grammar: Locative absolute: वर्षे गते 'the year having gone' = after a year. Noun and participle both in the locative.
Dual again: मूलकलान्तराभ्याम् 'from the two, principal and interest', ablative dual.
Mula = principal: the same word means root of a plant, square root (bee verse) and the principal of a loan.
question: What is the interest on 16 after one year? (Give a decimal.)
solution:
Rule of three (त्रैराशिक): if 100 earns 5 in 1 month, then 16 earns (16 × 5 × 12) / (100 × 1) in 12 months.

= 960 / 100 = 9.6 = 9⅗

Time from principal P and interest I: t = (100 × I) / (P × 5) months. Principal from time and interest: P = (100 × I) / (5 × t).

Science link: this is simple interest, I = P × r × t, with r = 5% a month. Bhaskara's rule of three (trairashika) is direct proportion, the same reasoning behind Ohm's law scaling: double the voltage, double the current.
